name: Ping-pong delay filtered motion recipe
goal: Build a musical ping-pong (L↔R bouncing) delay for synths/pads: tempo-synced time, moderate feedback, low wet mix, band-limit the repeats, optional saturation, even or offset L/R times, prefer send vs insert, and automate/modulate for evolving motion.

source.title: What Are The Best Ping-Pong Delay Techniques? - Music Producer Mastery

prerequisites: Stereo delay with ping-pong or independent L/R times; optional EQ/filter and saturation on delay path (FX bus order: EQ→chorus→delay→reverb)

inputs.name: routing
inputs.description: send (preferred for processing wet) vs insert

outputs.name: ping_pong_fx_rack
outputs.description: Configured bounce delay with filtered wet path

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Ableton/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Place delay in Traveler-style FX order after EQ/chorus and before reverb when building a cinematic bus.

steps.action: Enable ping-pong / stereo bounce delay. Set delay time to a musical subdivision (quarter or eighth) so repeats lock to groove.
Set feedback ~40–50% so repeats fade without clutter; wet/dry ~15–25% as a starting mix.
Filter the delayed signal: cut lows below ~100 Hz and highs above ~3 kHz to avoid mud/harshness. Optionally add tiny saturation/distortion on wet for warmth.
Maximize stereo width of the bounce when desired; link L/R times for even bounce, or slightly offset L vs R times for a more complex image.
Prefer send routing so you can EQ/compress the wet alone before blend; if insert, mind wet/dry carefully.

Automate or modulate feedback, delay time, or filter cutoff across sections; optional subtle chorus/flanger on delayed signal only. Use on synths (also vocals/guitars/perc) especially in sparse/breakdown sections.

verification: Repeats bounce L↔R in time with tempo
Wet path is band-limited (~100 Hz–3 kHz) and ~15–25% mix
Feedback does not build into clutter
